# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, common environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# Excludes loopback and docker bridge from TCP BTL (Byte Transfer Layer)
# Disables OpenIB BTL to prevent attempts to use InfiniBand hardware
# Disables a shared memory mechanism that can cause issues in some container runtimes
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_exclude=lo,docker0
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and certificates in a single layer
# git and wget for fetching source, build-essential for compiling, ca-certificates for secure connections
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a build directory
WORKDIR /build

# Build and install dependencies and the application in a single RUN layer to optimize image size
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt \
    #
    # --- METIS 4.0.3 ---
    #
    # Download METIS source from the specified URL
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -zxvf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    # Build METIS with specified OPTFLAGS to suppress implicit function declaration errors
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install the library and header as this METIS version lacks a 'make install' target
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    #
    # --- HYPRE 2.28.0 ---
    #
    # Download HYPRE source
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -zxvf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    # Perform an in-source build as required by HYPRE's build system.
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    # FIX: Manually copy the library and all headers as 'make install' is incomplete for this version.
    cp lib/libHYPRE.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp HYPRE_config.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cp hypre/include/*.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    #
    # --- MFEM 4.7 ---
    #
    # Clone MFEM source and checkout the specified version
    git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    git checkout v4.7 && \
    # Explicitly enable HYPRE/METIS and provide their install paths to the mfem build system.
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local MFEM_USE_METIS_5=NO MFEM_USE_METIS=YES METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    #
    # --- Laghos ---
    #
    # Clone Laghos source
    git clone https://github.com/ceed/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # Build Laghos in parallel, linking against the MFEM library installation
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    #
    # --- Final Setup ---
    #
    # Copy the compiled Laghos executable to a system path
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    # Create a final working directory and copy the necessary data files into it
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp -r data/* /app/ && \
    # Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size
    rm -rf /build

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Set the default command to run the Laghos application
CMD ["laghos"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed for a single-node CPU execution
# of the Laghos HPC mini-app on an AWS Kubernetes instance.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the experiment.
  name: laghos-cpu-experiment
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The size of the MiniCluster, corresponding to the number of pods.
  # Set to 1 to ensure the entire job runs on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks for the job.
  # This value is passed to `flux run -n`. A small number is chosen for a single-node run.
  tasks: 4

  # The main container specification that runs the application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
      
      # The launcher pod is explicitly disabled. The Flux Operator will
      # manage the job execution within this single container type.
      launcher: false
      
      # The command that will be executed by Flux.
      # The Flux Operator automatically prepends `flux run -n <tasks>`.
      # We are running the laghos binary with problem 1 (-p 1) on the specified mesh file.
      command: laghos -p 1 -m cube_311_hex.mesh
      
      # Set the working directory to where the mesh files are located inside the container.
      workingDir: /opt/laghos/data

  # Pods and resources will not be cleaned up upon job completion,
  # allowing for post-run inspection of logs and artifacts.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

# This revised MiniCluster manifest corrects the file path issue from the
# previous attempt and increases task count for better resource utilization.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the experiment.
  name: laghos-cpu-experiment-fix
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The size of the MiniCluster, corresponding to the number of pods.
  # Set to 1 to ensure the entire job runs on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks for the job, increased to utilize
  # more of the available CPU resources on a typical cloud instance.
  tasks: 64

  # The main container specification that runs the application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos

      # The launcher pod is explicitly disabled. The Flux Operator will
      # manage the job execution within this single container type.
      launcher: false

      # The command that will be executed by Flux.
      # The Flux Operator automatically prepends `flux run -n <tasks>`.
      command: laghos -p 1 -m cube_311_hex.mesh

      # Fix: The working directory is corrected to '/app', where the Dockerfile
      # places the application and its data files, resolving the
      # "Mesh file not found" error.
      workingDir: /app

  # Pods and resources will not be cleaned up upon job completion,
  # allowing for post-run inspection of logs and artifacts.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

# This MiniCluster manifest is corrected to resolve the Flux scheduler's "unsatisfiable request"
# error by explicitly scheduling the pod on a node with sufficient CPU resources.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for this corrected experiment run.
  name: laghos-cpu-experiment-final-fix
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Ensure the entire job runs on a single node pod.
  size: 1
  # Request 64 tasks to fully utilize the target instance's cores.
  tasks: 64

  # Pod specification to control scheduling.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      # Fix: Target a 'c7g.16xlarge' instance which has 64 vCPUs, ensuring
      # the 'tasks: 64' request can be satisfied by the Flux scheduler.
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7g.16xlarge

  # Flux-specific settings required for the target architecture.
  flux:
    container:
      # Fix: Use the ARM-compatible Flux image, as 'c7g' instances are ARM-based (Graviton).
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # The main application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
      launcher: false
      # Optimization: Add the '-pa' flag to enable partial assembly for improved performance.
      command: laghos -p 1 -m cube_311_hex.mesh -pa
      # Correct working directory where the input mesh file is located.
      workingDir: /app

  # Pods and resources will not be cleaned up upon job completion
  # to allow for post-run inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Enforce strict schema validation for the CRD.
  logging:
    strict: true

context.details:
Build laghos, building hyre, metis, and mfem from source first. 
You MUST install hypre 2.28.0 and disable fortran and add the --enable-bigint flag.
You MUST install metis 4.0.3 from https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz and add OPTFLAGS=-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration.
You MUST install mfem 4.7 and make parallel.
You MUST ensure all globbed files from ./data from the root of the laghos codebase are in the WORKDIR.
